method: tiny .abc probes -> abc2xml -o . -> xml.etree element counts (attribute-order independent); MuseScore 4 headless import smoke-test on every probe (all 8 IMPORT-OK when run individually; batch runs are flaky at the mscore-launch level, not content level)

3 <grace> elements with empty attribute dict (no slash), 0 slashed, no <duration> on grace notes; MuseScore 4 import OK

features.evidence: per group: 2 <grace> notes, second also carries <chord/>; 4 grace notes total for 2 groups; MuseScore 4 import OK
4 consecutive <grace> notes (D5 E5 F5 G5) then principal C5, all type=eighth, none with duration; MuseScore 4 import OK

features.feature: acciaccatura slash on multi-note grace run {/XY}
features.evidence: only 1 of 2 grace notes in the {/de} group carries slash="yes" (the first; s.acciatura is cleared after the first note at abc2xml.py:1102) - MuseScore's own MusicXML export puts slash="yes" on every note of a slashed run, so the rest of the run silently loses the acciaccatura flag

features.feature: grace-after (grace notes attached to the PRECEDING note, MusicXML <grace steal-time-previous>)
features.syntax: none exists. Probe c{d}| shows a trailing brace group is just emitted as a normal forward-attaching grace at that stream position
features.evidence: grep 'steal' over abc2xml.py = 0 hits; probe output: final <note> is a bare <grace> (no steal-time-previous attribute) stranded after the last principal note, which MusicXML semantics attach FORWARD to a following note that does not exist
features.proposal: extend the brace-group flag position already used by '/': a leading '<' inside braces, e.g. c{<d} -> emit the group's notes AFTER the principal note in document order with <grace steal-time-previous="50"> (mirrors acciaccatura = Literal('/') at abc2xml.py:172; '<' is unused inside braces so no grammar conflict with broken rhythm)

features.syntax: !arpeggio![ceg]  (decoration; handled at abc2xml.py:1412, not listed in FEATURES.md)
features.evidence: 2 decorated chords -> exactly 2 <arpeggiate number="1"/> inside <notations>, undecorated middle chord gets none, 0 phantom other-articulation; MuseScore 4 import OK. Caveat: element lands only on the FIRST chord note - MusicXML best practice (and MuseScore's own export) repeats <arpeggiate> on every chord note; MuseScore imports the first-note-only form fine

features.syntax: none exists (tried !arpeggioup! / !arpeggiodown!; no directional token in code or docs)
features.evidence: 0 <arpeggiate> elements in output; instead the two unknown tokens trigger the sticky phantom bug: 17 empty <other-articulation> elements sprayed over all 10 notes incl. the rest (notes 0-2 carry 1 each, notes 3-9 carry 2 each - each unknown deco permanently adds one more, same mechanism as D31/D95)
features.proposal: !arpeggioup! / !arpeggiodown! -> <arpeggiate direction="up|down" number="1"/>, added beside the existing 'arpeggio' branch at abc2xml.py:1412

features.evidence: 0 <non-arpeggiate> elements; identical phantom fallout to p07: 17 empty <other-articulation> elements across all 10 notes
features.proposal: !nonarpeggio![ceg] -> <non-arpeggiate type="bottom"/> on the lowest chord note and <non-arpeggiate type="top"/> on the highest (MusicXML defines the bracket by its two ends)

cross_cutting_observations: The unknown-decoration fallback (abc2xml.py:1453-1459 else-branch feeding staffDecos + other-articulation) is STICKY and CUMULATIVE: every unrecognised !token! adds one more empty <other-articulation> to every subsequent note in the voice, including rests. Measured in p07/p08: 1 unknown token -> +1 per note, 2 tokens -> +2 per note (17 total over 10 notes). This is the same mechanism family as known bugs D31 (!glissando!) and D95 (~).
Grace notes correctly omit <duration> and carry <type>eighth by default; <grace> is the first child of <note> as required.

MuseScore 4 headless (mscore -o out.mscz in.xml) is flaky when invoked in rapid succession - batch runs intermittently fail on random files; each of the 8 probes imports cleanly when retried individually. Do not trust a single batch FAIL.
